article.story: LAHAINA, Hawaii -- — Collin Chandler scored 18 of his 24 points in the second half and made two free throws in the final second as No. 19 BYU held off Providence 85-82 on Wednesday to take third place at the Maui Invitational. Tyler Betsey hit six 3-pointers and scored 22 points for the Cougars (7-1), who went 17 of 38 from beyond the arc. Bruce Branch III added 13 points. Chandler finished with six assists and went 7 for 7 at the line. Arrinten Page led Providence (5-3) with 20 points and five assists. Malik Mack had 17 points and eight assists. Jacob Bannarbie added 13 points. Mack’s 3-pointer gave Providence its last lead at 67-65 with 9:53 remaining. Chandler answered with a 3-pointer 23 seconds later, and BYU stretched its lead to 78-71 on Betsey’s sixth 3 with 4:05 left. Elijah Saunders hit a 3 to pull Providence within two before Jaxon Kohler answered to put BYU up 81-76 with 1:01 remaining. Page’s 3-pointer with two seconds left cut the deficit to 83-82. Chandler made both free throws after Gavin Hightower fouled him, and Page missed a buzzer-beater 3-pointer. Providence led by nine in the first half, but the teams went into halftime tied at 43 after combining for 17 3-pointers. The Friars shot 57.1% from the field, but BYU scored 13 second-chance points to Providence’s three and outscored the Friars 12-4 at the free-throw line. Up next BYU faces Northwestern on Dec. 5 in Salt Lake City. Providence hosts Stonehill on Tuesday. ------ Sign up for Top 25 poll alerts here, visit the Top 25 here and see AP’s full men’s basketball coverage here
